name: Steve Reich
hook: A composer who let two tape loops of a preacher drift out of step, and heard a new kind of music in the gap.

blurb.age13: Steve Reich was born in New York in 1936. In 1965 he made 'It's Gonna Rain' from a recording of a street preacher in San Francisco. He played the same short loop on two tape machines at once. Because the machines ran at slightly different speeds, the loops slowly drifted apart and made new rhythms and echoes. Brian Eno has said that hearing it was his first taste of the kind of music that became ambient.
blurb.adult: Born in New York in 1936. 'It's Gonna Rain' (1965) phases two copies of a tape loop of Brother Walter, a Pentecostal preacher recorded in Union Square, San Francisco, in 1964, on two Wollensak machines running at slightly different speeds. Reich then moved the same process to live players ('Piano Phase', 1967) and to large ensembles ('Music for 18 Musicians', ECM, 1978). He played in the 1964 premiere of Riley's 'In C' and suggested its pulse. Eno has cited 'It's Gonna Rain' in lectures as his first encounter with minimalism. The Orb's 'Little Fluffy Clouds' (1990) samples Pat Metheny's recording of Reich's 'Electric Counterpoint' (1987).
